heading: Lower magnitude-aware sharpness (weight-scaled sensitivity) correlates with smaller generalization gaps in restricted CNN comparisons
definition: among networks of one convolutional family trained to similarly low training loss, those that tolerate larger weight perturbations (scaled to the weights' magnitudes) before training error rises tend to have smaller gaps between training and test error, and this measure ranks the gaps better than the tested norm- and margin-based measures (CIFAR-10 and SVHN without data augmentation; Jiang et al. 2020). Sharpness alone fails some comparisons (Neyshabur et al. 2017); the relation is correlational.
summary: A separate study of CIFAR-10 CNNs with low loss supports this correlation using a related estimate of sharpness. How well sharpness ranks models by generalization remains unsettled: it failed in one comparison across depths, and normalized margins—measures of separation from the decision boundary adjusted for model scale—ranked models better in an extended test.

suggested_status.by_scale: C for broader magnitude-aware ranking claims in size-unspecified model collections; R2 for restricted CNN associations measured with related estimators, without establishing exact V7 reproduction. ? at explicitly labelled <1B scale: the audio evidence does not test V7's specified estimator. No size-resolved status at 1–10B, 10–100B or >100B.
suggested_status.reason: Independent low-training-loss CIFAR-10 CNNs without augmentation support the association through a modified log-likelihood-tolerance estimator (arXiv:2009.12789#R1). Extended DEMOGEN tests magnitude-aware Gaussian perturbation robustness using an expected-loss tolerance, a T2 related-estimator test rather than exact reproduction. Its association is positive, but normalized margins—an additional comparator not tested in the original—rank better (arXiv:2103.06002#R3). C rests on related NiN magnitude-aware-flatness ranking failure for depth 4-to-5 comparisons, predominantly on CIFAR-10, rather than demonstrated failure of the exact original pooled protocol (arXiv:2010.11924#R5). The audio study measures fixed-radius, filter-normalized loss sharpness; it is T6/discusses with no V7 verdict and supplies neither replication nor failure evidence (arXiv:2309.16369#R1; arXiv:2309.16369#R2). counts: versions.V7.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=0; versions.V7.studies_by_size contains '<1B' and 'not stated'. These script counts precede the checker corrections and do not establish a scale-specific replication.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent reproduction of the exact CIFAR-10/SVHN tolerance and comparator protocol, with matched training loss and no augmentation, could clarify the narrow claim's status. Reporting conditional results by depth, width and training recipe would distinguish aggregate tracking from intervention-specific failure. Explicit parameter sizes are needed for scale-specific status.

source.title: Fantastic Generalization Measures and Where to Find Them
source.authors: Yiding Jiang; Behnam Neyshabur; H. Mobahi; Dilip Krishnan; Samy Bengio

original_result.setup: They measured magnitude-aware sharpness—how much loss can rise when weights are perturbed on a scale set by their magnitudes—across hyperparameter configurations on CIFAR-10 and SVHN without data augmentation.
original_result.result: Magnitude-aware sharpness correlated with the generalization gap: Kendall τ = 0.484 on CIFAR-10 and 0.5676 on SVHN. The corresponding granulated correlations Ψ, which average correlations from comparisons that vary one hyperparameter at a time, were 0.516 and 0.5173.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: The reported flatness ranking advantage for WMT14 Transformers remains unverified.
Normalized sharpness tracked larger generalization gaps across tested random-label mixtures.
Flatter segmentation networks generalized better at matched training MSE.
Flatter committee machines (networks combining predictors) and ResNet-18 solutions had smaller generalization gaps in tested settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracked CIFAR-10 accuracy gaps better than the tested path norm.
Magnitude-aware flatness ranked generalization gaps well when depth increased from three to four.
Relative perturbation loss tracked ResNet18 generalization differences across weight-decay schedules.
Tuned adaptive sharpness tracked generalization gaps across tested WideResNet configurations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracked gaps in breast-ultrasound classifiers trained to low classification error.
Greater relative perturbation tolerance accompanied smaller gaps across extended DEMOGEN convolutional models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracked generalization on average across the tested dataset–architecture groups.
Greater perturbation robustness accompanied lower test error in continuous and binary convolutional networks.
Overall, higher values of magnitude-aware sharpness variants accompanied larger generalization gaps.
Connectivity sensitivity and adaptive sharpness tracked gaps in augmented CIFAR-10 VGG models.
Adaptive sharpness tracked ResNet-18 generalization within fixed augmentation and mixup settings.
SAM-all and ASAM-all paired lower adaptive sharpness with higher CIFAR-100 test accuracy.
Higher sharpness accompanied worse held-out performance for several multi-task learning comparisons.
Geodesically flatter BERT models had smaller MNLI generalization gaps.
Magnitude-aware curvature tracked larger reported gaps in modified ResNet-18 models.
Adaptive sharpness tracked ResNet18 gaps more strongly than parameter L2 norm.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracked loss gaps across convolutional model configurations when their results were combined.
Adaptive sharpness tracked gaps within each tested optimizer at fixed learning rates.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracked larger CIFAR-100 gaps across clean width and depth sweeps.
Reported Transformer flatness ranking disadvantages across widths and epochs remain unverified.
Sharpness tracking weakened or reversed when gap definitions and training settings changed.
Magnitude-aware flatness failed to rank gaps correctly across every tested intervention.
Reported DenseNet121 flatness failures at large perturbation strengths remain unverified.
Adaptive sharpness tracked gaps weakly when dropout varied.
Early-stopped ultrasound models showed negative sharpness–gap correlations with unequal training errors.
Normalized margins ranked generalization gaps better than magnitude-aware perturbation robustness on extended DEMOGEN.
Random perturbations tracked batch-size generalization differences less strongly than worst-case perturbations.
Reported Transformer flatness ranking disadvantages remain unverified across epochs and widths.
Reported sharpness ranking differences across individual hyperparameters remain unverified.
Original magnitude-aware measures tracked gaps less strongly than Fisher-Rao in augmented CIFAR-10.
Adaptive sharpness failed to rank ResNet-18 generalization consistently across augmentation and mixup settings.
Normalization-only SAM and ASAM improved accuracy despite higher measured adaptive sharpness.
Sharper audio CNNs had higher accuracy under a different loss-sharpness estimator.
Several multi-task models improved held-out performance despite increased adaptive sharpness.
Reported weak and reversed ASAM associations across augmented image-classification sweeps remain unverified.
Curvature tracking weakened for VGG-16 and failed across ResNet-18 augmentation protocols.
Reported inverse-margin ranking advantages over magnitude-aware flatness remain unverified.

Some comparisons within tested conditions reversed sharpness's overall positive association with generalization gaps.

Sharpness–gap correlations were not significant for Normalized Muon, SGD, and Adam under linear decay.

untested.what: An independent reproduction of the full original SVHN protocol combining the exact tolerance statistic, similarly low training loss, no augmentation and the original norm/margin comparison.
untested.basis: The original baseline is arXiv:1912.02178#R2. Pack untested-parts lines for arXiv:2009.12789 retain missing within-family SVHN or controlled comparisons. arXiv:2103.06002#R3 uses magnitude-aware Gaussian random-perturbation robustness with an expected-loss tolerance, a related estimator rather than a reproduction of the original sharpness statistic; its exact low-training-loss, no-augmentation protocol and SVHN are not separately tested. arXiv:2010.11924#R6 tests robust prediction with a related measure. arXiv:2606.08308, Section 5, specifies standard convolutional networks, including a modified AlexNet, but leaves exact architecture configurations, dataset assignments, training-loss matching and augmentation unspecified. counts: versions.V7.studies_by_family and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation describe broad coverage, not this conjunction.

wording_issues.phrase: this measure ranks the gaps better than the tested norm- and margin-based measures
wording_issues.issue: Keep this tied to the original comparison suite and protocol. Normalized margins win in extended DEMOGEN, whose magnitude-aware Gaussian random-perturbation measure uses an expected-loss tolerance rather than reproducing the original sharpness statistic. Path norm wins for information-bottleneck log-loss gaps; WMT14 rankings depend on the varied hyperparameter; the Fourier-study verdict reports higher inverse-margin correlations on its convolutional datasets.

wording_issues.phrase: among networks of one convolutional family
wording_issues.issue: A shared family alone does not define a reliable comparison group: augmentation/mixup and normalization-only optimizer variants can change tracking within convolutional families. For pooled retained CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 models, logit-normalized adaptive worst-case ℓ∞ sharpness has Kendall τ=0.29 at radius ρ=0.0005; this is not exclusively a between-subgroup coefficient. Under linear learning-rate decay, Normalized Muon, Coupled SGD and Coupled Adam lack significant ASAM–gap correlations, but comparable low training loss is unverified. Those schedule results limit transfer without establishing failure under V7's prerequisites. The no-augmentation restriction remains material.

wording_issues.phrase: trained to similarly low training loss
wording_issues.issue: Several extensions establish high training accuracy or near-zero training error rather than matched objective loss. ASAM's aggregate and batch-size, learning-rate and weight-decay results show tracking, while its dropout result is partial; these outcomes do not establish matched loss. Early-stopped single-task and multi-task BUSIS models have unequal training errors, with shallow single-task models underfitting; multi-task complexity measures cover only the classification branch. Their negative correlations leave scoped V7 cannot_determine and warrant no limits_scope verdict on its training-fit condition.

wording_issues.phrase: tolerate larger weight perturbations (scaled to the weights' magnitudes) before training error rises
wording_issues.issue: Many positive extensions measure loss at a fixed perturbation radius, expected local energy, output sensitivity or relative curvature. They support related magnitude-aware associations without reproducing the finite training-error tolerance statistic.

wording_issues.phrase: gaps between training and test error
wording_issues.issue: Extensions use log-loss gaps, MSE gaps, BLEU-based gaps or held-out task performance at comparable loss. The information-bottleneck study reports accuracy-gap τ=0.385 for its low-training-loss CIFAR-10 CNNs; switching to log-loss gaps changes correlation strength and the norm comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: Sharpness alone fails some comparisons (Neyshabur et al. 2017)
wording_issues.issue: The Neyshabur baseline varies CIFAR-10 training-set size within a fixed modified VGG architecture and already uses magnitude-dependent perturbations; random-label models have lower sharpness in smaller-training-set comparisons. Later magnitude-aware-flatness depth comparisons perform well from depth 3 to 4, fail from 4 to 5, and permit no conclusion from 5 to 6; almost all failing environments are CIFAR-10. Linear-decay results with unverified comparable training loss and BERT/CLIP transformer results limit extensions rather than contradicting V7 in its stated setting. The caveat should distinguish these conditions and should not imply that earlier failures concern only unscaled sharpness.

wording_issues.phrase: tolerate larger weight perturbations (scaled to the weights' magnitudes) before training error rises
wording_issues.issue: The audio study discusses a related construct: fixed-radius, filter-normalized, two-dimensional loss sharpness against test accuracy. It reports nearly 100% training accuracy and interprets one minus test accuracy as the generalization gap. Its reversed association concerns that loss-sharpness estimator; V7's perturbation-tolerance statistic and comparative ranking remain untested. The result leaves scoped V7 cannot_determine and supplies no limits_scope verdict.

method_sensitivity.what: On augmented CIFAR-10 WideResNet-28-2, ordinary/adaptive sharpness τ changes from 0.174 to 0.636 for p=2 and from 0.257 to 0.616 for p=∞. For adaptive p=∞ sharpness, conditional coefficients are 0.817 for batch size, 0.806 for learning rate and 0.656 for weight decay, versus partial dropout tracking at 0.225; adaptive Ψ=0.626 versus ordinary Ψ=0.316. Kernel-only perturbations and batch-statistics normalization distinguish clustering variants. On augmented VGG models, Connectivity Sharpness τ=0.837 and adaptive sharpness 0.755 exceed Sharpness-Mag. 0.473 and Pacbayes-Mag. 0.636; Fisher-Rao gives 0.649.

method_sensitivity.factor: Varied hyperparameter and aggregate versus conditional evaluation
method_sensitivity.what: Positive aggregate rankings coexist with augmentation, width, depth and weight-decay reversals in the clustering thesis. Its augmentation reversals limit extension beyond V7's no-augmentation condition; the weight-decay reversal is separate counterevidence. In robust-measures comparisons, pacbayes.mag.flatness performs well for depth 3 to 4, completely fails for depth 4 to 5, and permits no conclusion for depth 5 to 6; almost all failing environments are CIFAR-10. Extended DEMOGEN's magnitude-aware Gaussian random-perturbation robustness, μ=1/σ² with expected-loss tolerance, has weaker association along width, augmentation, weight decay and depth than along dropout. This is a related estimator rather than reproduction of the original sharpness statistic.

CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 adaptive sharpness tracks within fixed augmentation × mixup groups but does not reliably extend across groups. For logit-normalized adaptive worst-case ℓ∞ sharpness, pooled Kendall τ=0.30 at ρ=0.001 and τ=0.29 at ρ=0.0005; these coefficients pool retained models rather than measuring exclusively between-group comparisons. Relative curvature also gives positive within-protocol associations while reversing the ordering between no augmentation and augmented protocols.

For the same low-training-loss CIFAR-10 CNN collection, sharpness beats path norm for the accuracy gap, τ=0.385 versus 0.347, but loses for the log-loss gap, 0.233 versus 0.357. WMT14 magnitude-aware flatness ranks first across learning-rate variation but poorly across width and below several norm/margin metrics across epochs.

method_sensitivity.factor: Perturbation strength and probe batch size
method_sensitivity.what: Large multiplicative gamma can obscure DenseNet121 early/late weight-decay differences. On the converged CIFAR model grid, approximate ASAM Kendall τ changes from 0.264 with probe batch 256 to 0.433 with the full dataset; granulated coefficients change from 0.194 to 0.411.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning-rate schedule and optimizer parameter subset
method_sensitivity.what: Fixed-LR within-optimizer correlations in the Muon study become nonsignificant under linear decay for Normalized Muon, Coupled SGD and Coupled Adam, and weaker for Decoupled Muon. Comparable low training loss is unverified, so these results limit schedule transfer rather than establish failure under V7's prerequisites. Normalization-only SAM/ASAM gives higher sharpness and better accuracy than all-parameter variants, although all-parameter variants improve both relative to SGD. For augmented CIFAR-100 WRN-28, at the Table 6 sharpness probe with 20 steps and ρ=0.003, SGD has test accuracy 80.71±0.2% and sharpness 0.071±0.000; ASAM-all has 83.25±0.2% and 0.048±0.001.

Medical-image magnitude-aware flatness is positively correlated in the converged unregularized experiment. In early-stopped regularized BUSIS experiments, gap correlations are τ=-0.372 for single-task models and -0.342 for multi-task models. Training errors are unequal, shallow single-task models underfit, and multi-task complexity measures cover only the classification branch. These negative correlations are outside V7's training-fit condition: state=cannot_determine, with no limits_scope verdict. The entropic-gradient study explicitly states that flatness/test-error correlation is not observed when compared minima have different training errors.

Relative-curvature tracking is stronger in modified ResNet-18 than VGG-16 or DenseNet-121. Geodesic sharpness reverses direction in diagonal regression and ImageNet CLIP ViT-B/32 but correlates positively on MNLI BERT, where ordinary adaptive sharpness finds no correlation. The diagonal-regression and transformer findings limit extensions beyond V7's convolutional CIFAR-10/SVHN setting; they do not challenge the claim under its stated conditions. Multi-task transfer can improve or worsen while adaptive sharpness increases, depending on task and auxiliary data.

The NLP study reports correlations varying across hyperparameter settings, Simpson's paradox with particularly large learning rates, and reversed trends for some metrics across model series. Figure 4 summarizes correlations calculated over training epochs separately within each hyperparameter setting; the correlation axis is within-model training progress. The generalization gap is training BLEU minus test BLEU. No numerical correlation specific to pacbayes_mag_flatness is stated.
